Its parent pressure may be any smooth periodic choice satisfying the residual and coercivity bounds, and the central amplitude need only remain nonzero and below $\lambda^{-3/4}$; the paper fixes the Poisson pressure and an attained normalization.
e02.lemma53.near-origin.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.seedNear_of_h51: The paper displays an upper amplitude bound and strict positivity of the coupling in (5.19). The formal result also gives relative seed error, a lower amplitude bound and quantitative coupling bounds, so it contains additional information about the localized seed.

e02.lemma53.forward-hypotheses.TorusEuler.exists_paper_hierarchy_invers: The statement takes smooth active-interval fields with $V$ transverse and satisfying the projected wave equation. It also requires the initial value and source to vanish off a closed set within $2\ell_*$ of the lattice, with period-one phase and the prescribed label-phase translation symmetry. The parent deformation and central-wave bounds are separate inputs.
e02.lemma53.forward-hypotheses.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_3: The paper allows $V$ and $f$ to be smooth only on $[t_0,T]$. The formal statement requires fields smooth on all of $[0,T]$ and then restricts the estimate to the active interval, so this statement alone covers a narrower class of data.

e02.lemma53.forward-bound.TorusEuler.exists_paper_hierarchy_invers: The order-$n$ norm of a supported transverse solution on $[t_0,T]$ is bounded by $C_n\mathsf D^{20}$ times the sum of the launch norm divided by $\gamma(t_0)$ and the active weighted source norm. The exponent $20$ is fixed for every derivative order. In this estimate $V$ already solves the forward equation.
e02.lemma53.forward-bound.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist: For a small enough radius, $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$ and $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|$, supported solutions satisfy $\|V\|_{[n],\gamma}\le C_n\mathsf D^{20}(\gamma(t_0)^{-1}\|V(t_0)\|_{[n]}+\|f\|_{[n],\gamma})$. The paper gives (5.20) for fields defined only on the active interval. This formal estimate uses fields smooth on all of $[0,T]$, so the numerical bound is retained under a stronger time-domain assumption.
e02.lemma53.forward-bound.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_3: Supported transverse solutions obey $\|V\|_{[n],\gamma}\le C_n\mathsf D^C(\gamma(t_0)^{-1}\|V(t_0)\|_{[n]}+\|f\|_{[n],\gamma})$. The paper gives (5.20) for fields smooth on $[t_0,T]$. The numbered formal statement assumes smoothness on $[0,T]$ before restricting to the active interval; its conclusion therefore does not by itself cover arbitrary active-interval data.

e02.lemma53.zero-start-hypotheses.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist: Assume $0\le t_0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\lambda=|\kappa(t_0,0)|\ge1$, smooth periodic $U$, both deformation and gradient bounds $\mathsf D$, velocity derivative bounds $R_n\mathsf D^j$, and a nonzero central seed with relative transverse growth at most $\mathsf D$ and normalized coupling at least $\mathsf D^{-1}$. Profiles are smooth on $[0,T]$ and satisfy phase and coupled lattice periodicity; support lies within $2\ell_*$ of lattice points. The transverse stability assumption is $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for every transverse homogeneous solution $\mathbf b$ and $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$.
e02.lemma53.zero-start-hypotheses.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_3: Assume a smooth odd solenoidal parent and smooth periodic pressure on $0<T\le1$, bands $2\mathsf D$ for $U$ and $4\mathsf D$ for its odd residual $R_U$, bounds $\|DU\|,\|DX\|,\|DX^{-1}\|\le\mathsf D$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\|R_U\|\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. Let $0\le t_0<T$, $\lambda=|\kappa(t_0,0)|\ge1$, and a nonzero transverse central seed satisfy $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$ and $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||\mathbf a|$. Every transverse homogeneous solution $\mathbf b$ must obey $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$. For small fixed $\ell_*$ and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, nearby seeds obey $|\mathbf a(t,a)|\le2|\mathbf a(t,0)|$ and positive coupling.

r3c8-lemma53-transverse-existence.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist: The strain and nonzero covector are smooth and phase independent, with $\kappa_t=-M^T\kappa$; source profiles satisfy the phase period and the coupled label-translation law. For a smooth source with zero phase mean, this result constructs a transverse solution of (5.15) with zero initial velocity and normalized pressure. The equation is $V_t+MV+\kappa\mathsf p_s=f$, with $\kappa\cdot V=0$, $\langle V\rangle_s=\langle\mathsf p\rangle_s=0$, and $V(0)=0$.
r3c8-lemma53-transverse-existence.TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.TransverseSoluti: The paper refers to the solution and its pressure. This theorem proves that two smooth solutions with the same forcing, zero initial velocity and zero phase mean for the pressure coincide. The existence theorem linked here supplies the pair.

e02.lemma53.transverse-pressure-bound.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist: The inverse under the central stability and parent assumptions controls both transverse velocity and the oscillatory pressure from the same force. The factor $\lambda$ on pressure expresses the inverse wave-number gain from solving for its phase derivative and taking a periodic primitive.
e02.lemma53.transverse-pressure-bound.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_3: The formal bound retains $\|V\|_{[n],\gamma}+\lambda\|\mathsf p\|_{[n],\gamma}$ for every zero-initial transverse solution with supported, centered forcing. It allows the broader parent pressure class and any nonzero central amplitude below $\lambda^{-3/4}$, without requiring the peak normalization in the paper.

e02.lemma53.leading-bound.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.exists_pap: For a supplied localized seed with smooth compatible continuation, the fixed radial envelope shape at every such radius gives $\|A_1\|_{[n],\gamma}+\lambda\|\mathsf p[A_1]\|_{[n],\gamma}\le C_n\mathsf D^{20}\lambda^{-5/4}$. The paper states (5.22) for its fixed admissible radial cutoff. The formal estimate uses one chosen envelope, so it preserves the bound for that choice without quantifying over every admissible cutoff.
e02.lemma53.leading-bound.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_3: The paper allows any fixed radial cutoff with the stated plateau and support. The formal leading-wave clause uses a particular admissible choice, retaining (5.22) for that envelope.

e02.lemma53.frame-bounds.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.norm_cofra: The formal statement gives $\|A_\perp\|\le\|D_aX\|$ for a restricted linear map. It treats the first bound only; inserting the parent deformation bound yields $\|A_\perp\|\le\mathsf D$.
The formal statement bounds the projected inverse by $\|(D_aX)^{-1}\|$. It treats the second inequality only. The parent inverse-deformation hypothesis gives the bound by $\mathsf D$.

e02.lemma53.coframe-coefficient-proof.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.transverseCofra: Given Lemma D.2’s product estimate and smooth coefficient bounds $\|D^jc\|\le W_j\mathsf D^{16(j+1)}$, the formal conclusion bounds $G(I-P_\kappa)$ and $-2G(I-P_\kappa)MF$ with exponents $32(j+1)$ and $64(j+1)$. The paper uses the Gram-matrix inverse in coordinates on $\mathbb R^2$. The forward frame is not separately bounded by this declaration, and no inverse relation between $F,G$ is assumed.

e02.lemma53.gronwall.TorusEuler.weighted_near_label_forward: The formal statement treats any real normed-space homogeneous equation with a positive continuously differentiable weight, a central propagation factor $K>0$, coefficient perturbation at most $K^{-1}$ and interval length at most one. It gives factor $eK$; the paper’s application takes $K=\mathsf D^3$.

e02.lemma53.forced-integral.TorusEuler.weighted_near_label_forced_no: The formal estimate applies to a general forced linear equation with continuous coefficients and forcing, positive continuously differentiable weight and perturbation at most $K^{-1}$ of a central equation with propagation factor $K$. Setting $K=\mathsf D^3$ and the initial time to $t_0$ gives the paper’s displayed bound.

e02.lemma53.near-seed-comparison.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.seedNear_of_h51: The paper bounds the relative seed error by $C\mathsf D^C\lVert a\rVert$. The formal conclusion gives an unspecified coefficient depending on $\mathsf D$, so its statement does not expose the uniform polynomial dependence used in this display.
e02.lemma53.near-seed-comparison.TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.SeedNear: The paper requires the relative-error coefficient to be an absolute power of $\mathsf D$. The formal condition leaves that coefficient free, so this condition alone does not assert the displayed polynomial dependence.

e02.lemma53.pressure-coefficient-route.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.rescaled_pressu: The formal statement bounds only $M(\ell_*a)$, $\kappa(\ell_*a)/\lambda$ and $\lambda^2/|\kappa(\ell_*a)|^2$, through each fixed order, by $C\mathsf D,C\mathsf D^2,C\mathsf D^4$. It assumes smooth coefficient bounds at scale $\mathsf D_0$, $\mathsf D_0^{64}\le\mathsf D$ and $\ell_*\mathsf D^{16}\le1$. The product and phase-primitive estimates invoked in the paper are still needed to obtain the pressure bound.

e02.lemma53.pressure-estimate.TorusEuler.oscillatoryPhasePressure_weig: The formal bound controls weighted derivatives of the normalized phase primitive using supplied coefficient, velocity and source bounds, for smooth centered one-periodic fields. It retains those coefficient constants explicitly. Inserting the parent estimates and summing the derivative bounds gives $C_n\mathsf D^C$ in (5.24). This theorem alone does not derive that parent power.

e02.lemma53.leading-proof-route.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.lemma_5_3_of_le: The paper obtains the leading estimate by applying (5.20) with zero forcing, followed by (5.24). The formal proof uses a separate homogeneous leading-wave estimate instead, so this step reaches the same bound without invoking those already assembled conclusions.

e02.lemma53.leading-homogeneous.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitude.SeedOn.pap: With $A_1=g\mathbf a F_h$ and $\mathsf p[A_1]=-2g(\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a)|\kappa|^{-2}P_h$, the formal statement proves $A_{1,t}+MA_1+\kappa\partial_s\mathsf p[A_1]=0$ on $[t_0,T]$. The paper states the homogeneous transverse identity for any fixed admissible cutoff. The formal statement proves it for the chosen envelope, a special case of the paper's statement.

e02.hierarchy.velocity-blocks.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Cd: The formal definition only reindexes a stored correction: the paper’s $C_p$ is stored at $p-1$. It does not assert $C_1=0$ or the total velocity formula. The first follows from the expansion conditions and the latter from the other linked equality.
e02.hierarchy.velocity-blocks.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Yd: The formal definition gives $Y_p=V_p+C_p$ with the shifted correction index. It supplies this component of the display, but neither $Z_p$ nor the total velocity nor $C_1=0$.
e02.hierarchy.velocity-blocks.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Zd: For an indexed family of profiles, the formal definition gives $Z_p=V_p+C_p+B_p$ in the paper's notation. The formal definition gives $Z_p=Y_p+B_p$. The other equalities and the convention $C_1=0$ are separate definitions or hypotheses.
e02.hierarchy.velocity-blocks.TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.velocity_eq: The formal equality gives $W=\sum_{p=1}^PZ_p+C_{P+1}$ for $P\ge1$, assuming $C_1=0$. The paper also lists the definitions of $Y_p,Z_p$ and states the convention. This theorem uses rather than proves that convention.

e02.hierarchy.level-placement.TorusEuler.hierarchy_completion_previous: The paper asserts a bound for $C_p$. The linked formal result checks only that the frequency exponents fit. The estimate of the correction itself is a separate step.
e02.hierarchy.level-placement.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Yd: The definition groups $V_p$ with the preceding curl correction as $Y_p=V_p+C_p$. It does not prove the frequency gain or the norm bound justifying that grouping; Lemma 5.5 and the exponent calculation supply those facts.

e02.hierarchy.first-mean-source.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.levelSource: The formal definition gives the general source at level two using the differentiated switched correction, and subtracts its activation term. Identifying it with the displayed unswitched expression requires the leading-wave cutoff identities. The definition alone does not state those time-derivative identities.
e02.hierarchy.first-mean-source.TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.levelSource_eq_s: The formal equality reconciles two finite-sum definitions of $H_p$ for $p\le P$. It does not itself turn the level-two linear term into the unswitched expression in (5.25). The leading-wave activation identity is still required.
e02.hierarchy.first-mean-source.TorusEuler.HierarchyOperators.sourceBefo: The formal definition gives the general source at level two using the differentiated switched correction, and subtracts its activation term. Identifying it with the displayed unswitched expression requires the leading-wave cutoff identities. The definition alone does not state those time-derivative identities.

e02.hierarchy.first-linear-mean-zero.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera: The coefficients of the linear relay are independent of the phase. Averaging can therefore pass through them to give the averages of the oscillatory terms themselves, all of which are zero under the theorem's hypotheses. This leaves the nonlinear terms for the mean equation.

e02.hierarchy.mean-fast-integration.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera: The paper applies phase integration by parts with $C_2=C[V_1]$ and the second factor also $V_1$. The formal statement allows any transverse zero-mean $V$ and an independent profile $Y$, giving the same identity for $C[V]$ and $Y$.

e02.hierarchy.first-residual-inclusion.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.meanSource: The first mean correction is indexed by $p=2$. Its source definition inserts $-R_U\circ X$ there, in the coordinates of the parent labels. The estimate in (5.10) is the separate reason that this extra term fits the first mean's size budget.
e02.hierarchy.first-residual-inclusion.TorusEuler.exists_parentResidualWeighted: The weighted residual estimate uses the parent's Fourier band to bound derivatives of $R_U$, then bounds derivatives of $R_U\circ X$ by the chain rule. At sufficiently small envelope radius the weights retain the original $\lambda^{-5/2}$ scale, which is the size needed in the first mean equation.

e02.hierarchy.quadratic-levels.TorusEuler.hierarchyAdvectionLevel: The phase derivative counts one level earlier than label advection. The formal index is $i+j$ for a label term and $i+j-1$ for a phase term, so at level $p$ the latter sum uses $i+j=p+1$. The positive indices used here make the subtraction ordinary.

e02.hierarchy.general-pre-source.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.levelSource: The source $H_p$ contains $(\partial_t+M)C_p+\mathbf d\mathsf p_{p-1}$ and the two interaction sums of (5.26). The quoted formula is the case $3\le p\le P$; the formal level-two definition additionally subtracts the activation correction.
e02.hierarchy.general-pre-source.TorusEuler.HierarchyOperators.sourceBefo: Here a stored correction at index $p-1$ is the paper’s $C_p$; subtraction of indices is truncated at zero, and the physical use is $p\ge2$. The quoted formula is the case $3\le p\le P$; the formal level-two definition additionally subtracts the activation correction.

e02.hierarchy.sources.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.oscSource: This definition takes $H_p$, subtracts its phase average and reverses the sign to produce the oscillatory forcing. The cancellation leaves that forcing with zero phase mean. The supplementary forcing from the newly solved mean is added in the next step.
e02.hierarchy.sources.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.meanSource: The formal definition gives the mean source $-\langle H_p\rangle_s-\mathbf1_{p=2}R_U\circ X$. It does not define the centered oscillatory source $f_p$ in the same display. That part is supplied by the separate oscillatory-source definition.
e02.hierarchy.sources.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: The formal definition gives the mean source $-\langle H_p\rangle_s-\mathbf1_{p=2}R_U\circ X$. It does not define the centered oscillatory source $f_p$ in the same display. That part is supplied by the separate oscillatory-source definition.

e02.hierarchy.supplementary-source.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.suppSource: The formal definition gives $f_p^S=-\sum_{i=2}^{p}(B_i\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY_{p+1-i}$, with $Y_j=V_j+C_j$ in paper notation. In particular, at $p=2$ it is $-(B_2\cdot\kappa)\partial_sV_1$ when $C_1=0$, the extra term in (1.12). The sum is empty below level two. At every included index $p+1-i\ge1$, so nonnegative-integer subtraction agrees with ordinary subtraction. For phase-independent $B_i,\kappa$ and differentiable periodic $Y_j$, its phase average vanishes. These properties are not imposed by the formula alone; they come from the geometric profiles and expansion equations.
e02.hierarchy.supplementary-source.TorusEuler.HierarchyOperators.meanPhaseA: The formal statement gives the positive advection sum $\sum_{i=2}^p(B_i\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY_{p+1-i}$ for $p\le P$. The supplementary source in the paper is its negative. The other linked definition supplies that sign.

e02.hierarchy.transverse-after-mean.TorusEuler.FiniteHierarchySolvers.constr: The formal statement identifies the recursively selected pair with the output of a supplied transverse solution operator for exactly $f_p+f_p^S$, whose average is zero. Existence of that physical operator is an input here, not a conclusion of this selection theorem.

r2.hierarchy.complete-current-field.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsExpansion: The formal condition requires $C_{p+1}=C[V_p]$ for retained levels. It does not retain $Q_p$ as a separate member of the family. The vector potential is evaluated inside the curl-correction operation. Thus the correction equality is explicit while the separate assignment of $Q_p$ is absent.
r2.hierarchy.complete-current-field.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Cd: The formal definition reindexes the stored correction as the paper’s $C_{p+1}$. It imposes neither $Q_p=Q[V_p]$ nor $C_{p+1}=C[V_p]$; the latter is a separate expansion condition.

e02.prop54.well-defined.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: For the prescribed parent and launch data, the numbered result supplies a smooth leading seed and then a finite expansion for any chosen seed and any $P\ge2$. Its uniqueness clause compares the fields through level $P$ and the corrections through $P+1$. The extra seed-existence clause gives a starting profile for the recurrence in (5.11), (5.27) and (5.28).
e02.prop54.well-defined.TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_5_4: For the prescribed parent and launch data, the numbered result supplies a smooth leading seed and then a finite expansion for any chosen seed and any $P\ge2$. Its uniqueness clause compares the fields through level $P$ and the corrections through $P+1$. The extra seed-existence clause gives a starting profile for the recurrence in (5.11), (5.27) and (5.28).
e02.prop54.well-defined.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: The paper asserts that the finite expansion is well defined. This formal definition builds profiles from supplied leading data and selected solves. Existence of the localized seed and uniqueness of the resulting expansion require separate results.

Given the finite expansion data, the theorem proves that their sums have the required divergence, momentum remainder and inactive support. It also identifies which completion survives at level $P+1$. Construction of data satisfying the finite recursion is the separate existence part of Proposition 5.4.

e02.prop54.velocity-pressure-sums.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: In the velocity equality, summing $Z_p=V_p+C_p+B_p$ through $P$ leaves a final correction $C_{P+1}$ to add. The alternative sum attaches $C_{p+1}$ to each generating oscillation $V_p$. Pressure is the sum of oscillatory and mean pressures at levels $1$ through $P$. The numbered proposition also supplies existence and uniqueness for the finite expansion and includes existence of its leading seed.
e02.prop54.velocity-pressure-sums.TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_5_4: In the velocity equality, summing $Z_p=V_p+C_p+B_p$ through $P$ leaves a final correction $C_{P+1}$ to add. The alternative sum attaches $C_{p+1}$ to each generating oscillation $V_p$. Pressure is the sum of oscillatory and mean pressures at levels $1$ through $P$. The numbered proposition also supplies existence and uniqueness for the finite expansion and includes existence of its leading seed.
e02.prop54.velocity-pressure-sums.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.expansion: The definition gives the sum $\sum_{p=1}^P(V_p+C_{p+1}+B_p)$ only. The regrouping with $Z_p$, the pressure sum and $\bar q_1=0$ require the other definitions and expansion conditions.
e02.prop54.velocity-pressure-sums.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.expansionPressure: The definition gives $\mathsf P=\sum_{p=1}^P(\mathsf p_p+\bar q_p)$ only. The velocity equalities and the normalization $\bar q_1=0$ are independent parts of the display.
e02.prop54.velocity-pressure-sums.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsExpansion: The formal condition includes the initial mean and pressure normalization and the recursion satisfied by retained profiles. The displayed total velocity and pressure are defined separately and the regrouping of the velocity sum is a further equality.
e02.prop54.velocity-pressure-sums.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: In the velocity equality, summing $Z_p=V_p+C_p+B_p$ through $P$ leaves a final correction $C_{P+1}$ to add. The alternative sum attaches $C_{p+1}$ to each generating oscillation $V_p$. Pressure is the sum of oscillatory and mean pressures at levels $1$ through $P$. This identity uses an already constructed family with the prescribed leading inactivity.

e02.prop54.divergence.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: The completed oscillatory terms $V_p+C_{p+1}$ are transported curls and the means $B_p$ satisfy the solenoidal constraint from the endpoint equation. Summing both parts gives zero total divergence with $\widetilde{\mathbf d}=\mathbf d+\kappa\partial_s$. This is the divergence used when evaluating the profiles in physical coordinates. The numbered proposition also supplies existence and uniqueness for the finite expansion and includes existence of its leading seed.
e02.prop54.divergence.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: The completed oscillatory terms $V_p+C_{p+1}$ are transported curls and the means $B_p$ satisfy the solenoidal constraint from the endpoint equation. Summing both parts gives zero total divergence with $\widetilde{\mathbf d}=\mathbf d+\kappa\partial_s$. This is the divergence used when evaluating the profiles in physical coordinates. This identity uses an already constructed family with the prescribed leading inactivity.

e02.prop54.residual.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: In (5.29), the level equations cancel the interaction terms through $P$ and the first mean equation absorbs the parent residual. The leftover terms are the finite-depth remainder $R_P$ and the switching term $S+C[S]$ with $S=\widetilde\chi^{\prime}A_1$. The identity compares exact profiles before numerical bounds are applied. The numbered proposition also supplies existence and uniqueness for the finite expansion and includes existence of its leading seed.
e02.prop54.residual.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: In (5.29), the level equations cancel the interaction terms through $P$ and the first mean equation absorbs the parent residual. The leftover terms are the finite-depth remainder $R_P$ and the switching term $S+C[S]$ with $S=\widetilde\chi^{\prime}A_1$. The identity compares exact profiles before numerical bounds are applied. This identity uses an already constructed family with the prescribed leading inactivity.

e02.prop54.phase-means.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: The transverse solve has zero phase mean. Its divergence correction is a label curl of the normalized phase primitive, whose mean stays zero under the phase-independent label operators. The explicit zero means of $V_p$ and $C_p$ therefore leave exactly the sum of $B_p$ as the mean of $W$. This identity uses an already constructed family with the prescribed leading inactivity.

e02.prop54.oscillatory-support.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: The assertion gives $W-\langle W\rangle_s=\sum_{p=1}^P(V_p+C_{p+1})$ and makes it vanish outside the envelope support. It also makes the transverse source vanish there at every retained correction level $2\le p\le P$. Outside that support, only mean products enter the preliminary source, and subtracting its phase mean removes them. The numbered proposition also supplies existence and uniqueness for the finite expansion and includes existence of its leading seed.
e02.prop54.oscillatory-support.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: The assertion gives $W-\langle W\rangle_s=\sum_{p=1}^P(V_p+C_{p+1})$ and makes it vanish outside the envelope support. It also makes the transverse source vanish there at every retained correction level $2\le p\le P$. Outside that support, only mean products enter the preliminary source, and subtracting its phase mean removes them. This identity uses an already constructed family with the prescribed leading inactivity.

e02.prop54.vanishing-prefix.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: Before $t_0$, the retained oscillatory velocities, phase pressures, transverse sources and attached divergence corrections all vanish on the time slab. The first oscillation vanishes by the cutoff, and the transverse solves at later levels preserve this zero prefix. The support clause ranges over the oscillatory fields and their sources, while the mean equations use the full time interval. The numbered proposition also supplies existence and uniqueness for the finite expansion and includes existence of its leading seed.
e02.prop54.vanishing-prefix.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: Before $t_0$, the retained oscillatory velocities, phase pressures, transverse sources and attached divergence corrections all vanish on the time slab. The first oscillation vanishes by the cutoff, and the transverse solves at later levels preserve this zero prefix. The support clause ranges over the oscillatory fields and their sources, while the mean equations use the full time interval. This identity uses an already constructed family with the prescribed leading inactivity.

e02.prop54.final-index.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: The correction generated by $V_P$ is retained at the last index. With $V_{P+1}=B_{P+1}=0$, both $Y_{P+1}$ and $Z_{P+1}$ are that correction. In the helper whose array stores $C[V_p]$ at index $p$, the stored $C_P$ is the paper’s $C_{P+1}$. The numbered proposition also supplies existence and uniqueness for the finite expansion and includes existence of its leading seed.
e02.prop54.final-index.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsExpansion: For $1\le p\le P$, $C_{p+1}=\mathbf d\times[-\partial_s^{-1}(\kappa\times V_p/|\kappa|^2)]$. For $2\le p\le P$, require $B_{p,t}+MB_p+\mathbf d\bar q_p=-\langle H_p\rangle_s-\mathbf1_{p=2}R$ and $V_{p,t}+MV_p+\kappa\mathsf p_{p,s}=-(H_p-\langle H_p\rangle_s)+f_p^S$. Here $H_p$ is the sum of the preceding linear correction and all lower-level quadratic interactions, with the activation correction subtracted at level two; $f_p^S=-\sum_{i=2}^p(B_i\cdot\kappa)\partial_s(V_{p+1-i}+C_{p+1-i})$. Means satisfy $B_p=DX\,z_{p,t}$, $\operatorname{div}_az_{p,t}=0$, $z_p(0)=z_p(T)=0$ and zero spatial pressure mean. Finally $V_{P+1}=B_{P+1}=0$.
e02.prop54.final-index.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: The correction generated by $V_P$ is retained at the last index. With $V_{P+1}=B_{P+1}=0$, both $Y_{P+1}$ and $Z_{P+1}$ are that correction. In the helper whose array stores $C[V_p]$ at index $p$, the stored $C_P$ is the paper’s $C_{P+1}$. This identity uses an already constructed family with the prescribed leading inactivity.

e02.prop54.tail.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.remainder: The stored correction is indexed by its generating velocity, so the paper’s $C_{P+1}$ is the stored correction with index $P$. The expression is (5.30): the two final linear terms, label interactions with $i+j\ge P+1$, and phase interactions with $i+j\ge P+2$. Both indices run through $P+1$, where only the final correction remains. The activation error is separate. The expansion equations are needed to identify this expression with the uncanceled momentum residual.
e02.prop54.tail.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi: The remainder starts with the linear contribution of $C_{P+1}$ and the label gradient of the last phase pressure. The label products use $i+j\ge P+1$, while the fast phase products use $i+j\ge P+2$ because the phase derivative lowers their assigned level by one. The switching term is accounted for separately in (5.29). This identity uses an already constructed family with the prescribed leading inactivity.
e02.prop54.tail.TorusEuler.HierarchyOperators.remainder: This is a definition for a finite profile family. The stored correction at index $p$ represents the paper’s $C_{p+1}$, rather than $C_p$. The remainder contains $(\partial_t+M)C_{P+1}+\mathbf d\mathsf p_P$ and the quadratic interactions beyond the retained depth, as in (5.30). Phase advection is separated into contributions from corrections and means because $V_i\cdot\kappa=0$. Both $u,R_u$ are odd and divergence free, with Fourier radii $2\Lambda,4\Lambda$. Set $\varepsilon=\Lambda^{2-P}(1+\|V\|_{C_tC^{P,1/2}})^2$ and $e=C\|R_V\|_{C_tC^{1,1/2}}+C_P\varepsilon$. Then $\|u-V\|_{C_tC^{2,1/2}}\le C_P\varepsilon$, $\|R_u\|_{C_tC^{1,1/2}}+\|D^2(p-\Pi)\|_{C_tC^{0,1/2}}\le e$, and $D^2(p-p_U)\le(s+e)I$. The exponent $2-P$ is signed integer arithmetic.

euler02.truncation.poisson-pressure.TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsTruncation: This condition identifies $u$ with $S_\Lambda V$ on $[0,T]$ by requiring the cutoff formula for every continuous function on $\mathbb T^3=\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$ representing $V$. At each time, $p$ must be smooth, periodic, have zero integral over the centered unit cell, and solve $\Delta p=-\operatorname{tr}((\nabla u)^2)$. Existence of a continuous periodic representative of $V$ is not included in this condition: without one, its cutoff clause alone imposes no restriction. The condition specifies the pressure spatially at each time; joint time smoothness is proved for the constructed truncation.
euler02.truncation.poisson-pressure.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: The new pressure is determined by a mean-zero Poisson problem for the truncated velocity. Its right side cancels the divergence of $u\cdot\nabla u$ when $\operatorname{div}u=0$. This selects the new pressure even though the previous approximate pressure had a different residual.
euler02.truncation.poisson-pressure.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage: A truncated stage supplies continuous torus representatives of $V$ and $R_V$, a velocity $u=S_\Lambda V$, and a smooth periodic pressure $p$ of zero spatial mean on $[0,T]$. It requires $u$ smooth, odd and divergence free, with Fourier support $|\xi|\le2\Lambda$, and $\Delta p=-\operatorname{tr}((\nabla u)^2)$. Its actual momentum residual is identified both with $u_t+\mathbb P\operatorname{div}(u\otimes u)$ and with the cutoff expression in (5.58).
euler02.truncation.poisson-pressure.TorusEuler.nonempty_truncatedChildStage: The theorem constructs the cutoff field and recovers its smooth periodic pressure with mean zero. Since the velocity is divergence free, the Poisson source is $-\operatorname{tr}((\nabla u)^2)$. Its spatial integral vanishes, so the zero-mean condition selects the unique periodic solution.
euler02.truncation.poisson-pressure.TorusEuler.periodicPoissonPressure_uniqu: The theorem identifies any two smooth periodic zero-mean pressures with equal Laplacians. It applies to any common source, but does not assert existence for $-\operatorname{tr}((\nabla u)^2)$. The other linked construction supplies that existence.

euler02.truncation.residual-definition.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: The residual is the actual momentum defect obtained by substituting the truncated velocity and its newly chosen pressure into Euler. This formula includes the time derivative, unlike the Poisson equation that sets the gradient part. Later bounds measure the size of this defect.
euler02.truncation.residual-definition.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.residual: For the truncated velocity $u$ and its smooth periodic zero-mean Poisson pressure $p$, define $R_u(t,x)=\partial_tu(t,x)+(u(t,x)\cdot\nabla)u(t,x)+\nabla p(t,x)$. The time derivative is taken within $[0,T]$, so the values at $0$ and $T$ use one-sided derivatives on that interval. The definition alone does not assert $R_u=0$, a norm bound, or a Fourier support bound; those are separate properties or estimates of the truncated stage.

euler02.truncation.velocity-properties.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: The smooth radial cutoff kills modes beyond $2\Lambda$. It commutes with spatial differentiation and reflection, preserving divergence freedom and oddness. The formal statement collects those properties for the child velocity over its whole stage.
euler02.truncation.velocity-properties.TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_5_11: The proof applies the smooth Fourier cutoff to the assembled velocity. The cutoff keeps only the band of radius $2\Lambda$, commutes with differentiation and preserves odd parity. The child therefore has the regularity and divergence properties required of the next parent.
euler02.truncation.velocity-properties.TorusEuler.nonempty_truncatedChildStage: The construction chooses the child velocity by applying the cutoff and chooses pressure from the corresponding Poisson equation. The velocity inherits oddness and zero divergence and has the required finite band. The numerical estimate of the change caused by truncation uses further bounds on the cutoff.
euler02.truncation.velocity-properties.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage: The paper asserts the properties of the constructed truncated velocity. The formal description at this link requires those properties of a truncated stage. Existence of such a stage is supplied by the accompanying construction and Proposition 5.11.

euler02.truncation.residual-properties.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: Both factors in the nonlinear velocity product have frequencies at most $2\Lambda$, so their product reaches at most $4\Lambda$. The pressure projection removes its gradient part, leaving a divergence-free residual. Oddness follows from the parity of the velocity and its derivatives.
euler02.truncation.residual-properties.TorusEuler.paperProposition511_physicalC: Let $P\ge2$, $T>0$, $\Lambda\ge1$, with $V,R_V$ smooth periodic fields, $V$ odd and divergence free, and a pressure $\Pi$ smooth and periodic at each time. Both $u,R_u$ are odd and divergence free, with Fourier radii $2\Lambda,4\Lambda$.

euler02.truncation.error-bounds.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: The first bound measures the direct Fourier-tail error in velocity. The second also includes the old momentum residual, since recomputing pressure and projecting the new momentum transfer part of that error. The formal result controls the sum of the two time-uniform error norms.
euler02.truncation.error-bounds.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_11_: The velocity difference comes from the Fourier tail and has the budget $\varepsilon_\Lambda$. The new momentum residual and the pressure Hessian difference also inherit an error from the old residual. Applying the projection and Poisson estimates to those two contributions gives the sum in (5.56).
euler02.truncation.error-bounds.TorusEuler.paperProposition511_physicalC: This cutoff theorem applies to any smooth periodic odd divergence-free approximation satisfying its momentum equation, rather than requiring the specific finite expansion. Its additional pressure hypothesis is an upper bound for $D^2(\Pi-p_U)$, used for the accompanying pressure conclusion. It yields the displayed cutoff estimates for those inputs.

euler02.truncation.pressure-upper.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5: The proof adds the Hessian of the pressure change $p-\Pi$ to the parent-relative Hessian of $\Pi$. The norm bound in (5.56) gives an upper bound on the first quadratic form. The bound from Lemma 5.9 gives the other term in (5.57).
euler02.truncation.pressure-upper.TorusEuler.paperProposition511_physicalC: This theorem assumes the upper bound for $D^2(\Pi-p_U)$ of the input approximation and adds the cutoff pressure error. It does not prove Lemma 5.9 or derive that input bound from the parent and hierarchy. The full proposition supplies this connection.

For a twice continuously differentiable vector field $u:\mathbb R^3	o\mathbb R^3$ with $\operatorname{div}u=0$ everywhere, $\operatorname{div}((u\cdot
abla)u)=\operatorname{tr}((
abla u)^2)$ at every point. The square is matrix composition, not the sum of the squared entries of $
abla u$. This identity follows by differentiating the product and using $u\cdot
abla\operatorname{div}u=0$. It is the spatial identity used in §5.7 to choose $\Delta p=-\operatorname{tr}((

euler02.truncation.projected-residual.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage: The formal description requires the projected-residual identity as a property of a truncated stage. It does not construct that stage or derive the identity. The linked existence theorem proves that the required objects and identity are available.
euler02.truncation.projected-residual.TorusEuler.nonempty_truncatedChildStage: The construction recovers pressure from the cutoff velocity itself. Its gradient cancels the gradient part of $\operatorname{div}(u\otimes u)$, leaving $\partial_tu+\mathbb P\operatorname{div}(u\otimes u)$ as the momentum residual. The same theorem supplies the smooth velocity and recovered pressure used in this identity.

euler02.truncation.residual-identity.TorusEuler.projected_residual_of_cutoff: The formal algebra assumes commutation of the cutoff with divergence, annihilation of pressure gradients by the projection, the approximate momentum equation and the cutoff identity for the time derivative. Expanding with $v_\Lambda=u-V$ then gives exactly (5.58). Establishing those analytic premises is separate.

euler-r2.truncation.quadratic-tensor-cos.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.exists_cutoffBo: The formal result bounds the cutoff errors by $\Lambda^{2-P}$ times the square of one plus the order-$P$ Hölder norm of $V$. The passage explains the derivative count underlying that budget. After projecting the divergence, an order-one residual estimate needs order two on the tensor, and its two velocity factors account for the square. The intermediate tensor bounds belong to the residual proof.

euler02.truncation.velocity-tail.TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalfNorm_cutoffV: The paper uses the tail estimate at orders $s\le2$. The formal result allows every integer order $s\le P$ and every $\Lambda>0$, so it includes the required range $P\ge2$, $\Lambda\ge1$.

euler02.truncation.holder-product.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_5_59: The paper states the product inequality (5.59). The formal statement covers every bounded bilinear product $B$, with the necessary factor $\|B\|$, and also concludes Hölder regularity of the product; scalar and tensor products are included.
euler02.truncation.holder-product.TorusEuler.Paper.Text.eq_5_59: The paper states the product inequality (5.59). The formal theorem covers every bounded bilinear product $B$, with the necessary factor $\|B\|$, and also concludes Hölder regularity of the product; scalar and tensor products are included.
euler02.truncation.holder-product.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.eq_5_59: The paper leaves $C_m$ unspecified in (5.59). The formal proof supplies $C_m=3(m+1)2^m$ and works for any bounded bilinear product, including its operator norm and the regularity of the output.
euler02.truncation.holder-product.TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_bilinear: The paper writes (5.59) for a product of fields. The formal estimate covers every bounded bilinear product, multiplying by its operator norm, so it applies uniformly to scalar multiplication and the required tensor operations.

euler-r2.truncation.tensor-estimate.TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.truncatedParent: The formal statement bounds the velocity tail in $C^{2,1/2}$ and the complete projected residual expression in $C^{1,1/2}$, assuming cutoff-tail, product and projection bounds. It does not separately state that each of the three tensors belongs to $C^{2,1/2}$ with the displayed size. Their individual estimates occur in the proof. The final residual bound also includes the projected cutoff of $R_V$, which is absent from the quoted tensor estimate.

euler02.truncation.pressure-poisson-diff.TorusEuler.divergence_gradient_cutoffPre: The formal conclusion is $\Delta(p-\Pi)=-\operatorname{tr}((\nabla u)^2-(\nabla V)^2)-\operatorname{div}R_V$. Writing $v_\Lambda=u-V$ expands the trace into the two terms displayed in the paper. The auxiliary divergence-free time term is general; in this application it is $V_t$.

euler02.truncation.final-upper-bound.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_11_: The cutoff proof combines two estimates. The parent-relative approximate pressure Hessian has the one-sided bound from Lemma 5.9. The Hessian of $p-\Pi$ has a norm bound from the cutoff, which also gives an upper bound as a quadratic form. Adding yields the child bound.
euler02.truncation.final-upper-bound.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.pressureH: The estimate treats $D^2(p-\Pi)$ as a symmetric error. A norm bound $B$ implies that its quadratic form is at most $B|v|^2$ on each $v$, giving $D^2p\le D^2\Pi+BI$. The additional bound on $D^2(\Pi-p_U)$ comes from Lemma 5.9.
euler02.truncation.final-upper-bound.TorusEuler.paperProposition511_physicalC: The physical cutoff theorem takes a one-sided bound on $D^2(\Pi-p_U)$ and estimates the difference between the new Poisson pressure and $\Pi$. Thus bounding the cutoff error in Hessian norm preserves the parent-relative upper bound up to an explicit additional scalar multiple of the identity.

r2-s6-rho-hypothesis.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_6_1: The formal statement uses exactly $0<\rho\le1$ for Lemma 6.1; the stationary shear formula itself is defined for every real $\rho$.

e03-s6-shear-formulas.TorusEuler.stationaryShear: Equation (6.1) gives both $U_0$ and its central gradient. This definition gives $U_0(x)=\sin(2\pi x_2)(e_1+\rho e_3)$ on $\mathbb R^3$ for every real $\rho$, but does not itself identify its derivative with $B_\rho$.
e03-s6-shear-formulas.TorusEuler.stationaryShearGradient: Equation (6.1) gives both $U_0$ and $B_\rho$. This definition gives only $B_\rho v=2\pi v_2(e_1+\rho e_3)$ for real $\rho$; the velocity formula and the proof that this is its gradient at zero are separate.

e03-s6-shear-regularity.TorusEuler.stationaryShear_base_T1: For the shear $U_0(x)=\sin(2\pi x_2)(e_1+\rho e_3)$, the formal theorem proves joint smoothness on $[0,1]\times\mathbb R^3$, integer periodicity, oddness and zero divergence for every real $\rho$, together with a Fourier-band bound when the initial frequency is at least one. The quoted clause uses only smoothness, oddness and zero divergence in the smaller range $0<\rho\le1$.

e03-s6-shear-fourier.TorusEuler.stationaryShear_mFourierCoeff: The paper asserts containment of the Fourier support of $U_0$ in $\{e_2,-e_2\}$. For every real $\rho$, the formal theorem says a Fourier coefficient is nonzero if and only if its frequency is one of those two vectors; both coefficients are therefore present.

e03-s6-no-second-component.TorusEuler.stationaryShear_second: The second component of $U_0(x)=\sin(2\pi x_2)(e_1+\rho e_3)$ is zero for every $x\in\mathbb R^3$ and every real $\rho$, extending the paragraph's restriction $0<\rho\le1$. The coordinate numbered one in the formal statement is the paper's second coordinate.

e03-s6-no-advection.TorusEuler.stationaryShear_advection: The formal theorem proves $D U_0(x)[U_0(x)]=0$ for every real $\rho$ and every $x\in\mathbb R^3$, where $U_0(x)=\sin(2\pi x_2)(e_1+\rho e_3)$. This is the stated advection identity with no restriction on the shear parameter.

e03-s6-zero-pressure-residual.TorusEuler.isEulerSolution_stationaryShe: For every real $\rho$ and every $T>0$, the formal theorem makes the stationary shear an unforced Euler solution on $[0,T)$ with pressure identically zero. Its momentum residual is therefore zero there. The paper uses this in the range $0<\rho\le1$; the formal result also includes smoothness, periodicity and incompressibility.

e03-s6-fixed-second-coordinate.TorusEuler.stationaryShearFlow_second: The explicit lifted trajectory satisfies $(X_0(t,a))_2=a_2$ for every real time, every label and every real $\rho$. The paper uses this identity on its positive-time interval and for $0<\rho\le1$.

e03-s6-flow-deformation.TorusEuler.stationaryShearFlow: The display supplies the trajectory and the two deformation formulas. The formal definition gives only $X_0(t,a)=a+t\sin(2\pi a_2)(e_1+\rho e_3)$, for all real $\rho,t$ and all labels. Its derivatives and inverse are proved separately.
e03-s6-flow-deformation.TorusEuler.stationaryShearFlow_jacobians: The formal theorem gives both $D_aX_0(t,a)=I+t\cos(2\pi a_2)B_\rho$ and $D_xX_0(-t,X_0(t,a))=I-t\cos(2\pi a_2)B_\rho$, for all real $\rho,t$. It uses the separately defined trajectory, whereas the display also states that trajectory explicitly.

e03-s6-square-zero.TorusEuler.stationaryShearGradient_sq: Applying $B_\rho=2\pi(e_1+\rho e_3)\otimes e_2$ twice introduces the scalar factor $e_2\cdot(e_1+\rho e_3)=0$. Thus $B_\rho^2=0$ for every real $\rho$. This is the identity that makes $I+cB_\rho$ invertible with inverse $I-cB_\rho$ in (6.2).

e03-s6-origin-fixed.TorusEuler.stationaryShearFlow_origin: The explicit shear flow satisfies $X_0(t,0)=0$ for all real $t$ and $\rho$. The paper applies the same identity on its construction interval and for $0<\rho\le1$.

e03-s6-gradient-bound.TorusEuler.norm_stationaryShearGradient_: The paper uses $0<\rho\le1$. The formal theorem gives the operator-norm bound $\|2\pi(e_1+\rho e_3)\otimes e_2\|\le4\pi$ for the larger range $|\rho|\le1$, including zero and negative tilt.

e03-s6-first-wave-choice.TorusEuler.FirstWaveOrigin: The paper prescribes $k_*=\lambda e_1$ and the time cutoff $\widetilde\chi\equiv1$. The formal description of the first central wave fixes $\kappa(0)=\lambda e_1$ but includes no time cutoff. At time zero the deformation is the identity, so the covector agrees with $k_*$; the constant cutoff is supplied elsewhere.

e03-s6-initial-couplings.TorusEuler.FirstWaveOrigin.initial_coupl: For a first central wave with $\lambda>0$ and initial amplitude a positive multiple of $e_2$, the formal result identifies its initial frame with $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ and proves both displayed couplings for every real $\rho$. The paper uses the same values for $0<\rho\le1$.

e03-s6-lemma61-origin.TorusEuler.paperLemma61_firstWave: Let $0<\rho\le1$, $\lambda>0$, $B_\rho=2\pi(e_1+\rho e_3)\otimes e_2$ and $T\|B_\rho\|\le1/8$. For every first central pair already supplied, The pair has $\kappa(0)=\lambda e_1$, $\mathbf a(0)=ce_2$ with $c>0$, remains nonzero and perpendicular, solves $\kappa_t=-B_\rho^T\kappa$, $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)B_\rho\mathbf a$ on $[0,T]$, and attains $\max|\mathbf a|=\lambda^{-3/4}$. Here $P_\kappa$ projects onto $\mathbb R\kappa$. Put $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a|$ and $\nu=(\kappa/|\kappa|)\cdot B_\rho(\mathbf a/|\mathbf a|)$. For every $\mathsf D\ge2$, every transverse solution of the same amplitude equation and $0\le t'\le t\le T$, the conclusions are $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ and $\nu(t)\ge\mathsf D^{-1}$. The formal statement also bounds the initial strength and permits $0<\lambda<1$, whereas the paper assumes $\lambda\ge1$.
e03-s6-lemma61-origin.TorusEuler.paperLemma61_exists_firstWave: The first wave starts in the explicit stationary shear. The short-time bound keeps its normalized first coupling positive and controls any other transverse solution relative to the normalized amplitude of the seed. These are the two estimates (5.5) needed to begin the induction.
e03-s6-lemma61-origin.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_6_1: The statement asks for two bounds under the short-time condition. The first is a lower bound for the central coupling. The second compares the growth of any transverse solution to the seed's amplitude. Both use the same launched first wave.
e03-s6-lemma61-origin.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_6_1: The first-wave proof controls the amplitude equations on a short interval using the explicit stationary shear. It keeps the first coupling above $\mathsf D^{-1}$ and bounds the relative growth of every transverse solution, so the first wave meets the two conditions needed to start later amplification.

e03-s6-lemma61-strength.TorusEuler.FirstWaveOrigin.initial_stren: The formal theorem gives $\lambda^{1/4}/2\le|\kappa(0)||\mathbf a(0)|\le\lambda^{1/4}$ for every normalized first wave with $\lambda>0$ and $T\|B_\rho\|\le1/8$, without restricting $\rho$. The paper assumes $0<\rho\le1$ and uses $\lambda\ge1$.
e03-s6-lemma61-strength.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_6_1: Under $0<\rho\le1$, $\lambda\ge1$, $T>0$ and $T\|B_\rho\|\le1/8$, the initial strength is $|\kappa(0)||\mathbf a(0)|$ and the formal statement gives exactly the displayed interval for every first wave with attained peak $\lambda^{-3/4}$.
e03-s6-lemma61-strength.TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_6_1: Under $0<\rho\le1$, $\lambda\ge1$, $T>0$ and $T\|B_\rho\|\le1/8$, the initial strength is $|\kappa(0)||\mathbf a(0)|$ and the formal statement gives exactly the displayed interval for every first wave with attained peak $\lambda^{-3/4}$.

e03-s6-weighted-propagation.TorusEuler.FirstWaveOrigin.weighted_forw: Let $B_\rho=2\pi(e_1+\rho e_3)\otimes e_2$, $\lambda>0$, and $T\|B_\rho\|\le1/8$. For a nonzero transverse seed solving the central wave equations with initial data $\kappa(0)=\lambda e_1$, $\mathbf a(0)=ce_2$, $c>0$, and attained maximum $\lambda^{-3/4}$ on $[0,T]$, put $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a|$. Every solution $\mathbf b_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)B_\rho\mathbf b$, with $P_\kappa$ the orthogonal projection onto $\mathbb R\kappa$, satisfies $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for every $\mathsf D\ge2$ and $0\le t'\le t\le T$. The formal statement includes amplitudes not assumed transverse but omits the intermediate exponential bound. These two changes justify the verdict different.
e03-s6-weighted-propagation.TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_6_1_of: Assume the frame identities of Lemma 2.2. Let $0<\rho\le1$, $\lambda\ge1$, $T>0$ and $T\|B_\rho\|\le1/8$, where $B_\rho=2\pi(e_1+\rho e_3)\otimes e_2$. For the first nonzero transverse central wave with $\kappa(0)=\lambda e_1$, initial amplitude in the positive $e_2$ direction and attained maximum $\lambda^{-3/4}$ on $[0,T]$, put $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a|$. e03-s6-normalized-time.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl: The formal definition is $\tau=r(t-t_0)$ for real time $t$. Here $r>0$ is fixed at activation, so $[t_0,T]$ is converted to a normalized interval of length $r(T-t_0)$.

e03-s6-activation-vector.TorusEuler.inverseAdjoint_activationWave: The paper chooses $k_*=\lambda(D_aX(t_0,0))^TE_3(t_0)$. The formal theorem instead proves $F^{-T}(\lambda F^TE_3)=\lambda E_3$ for any invertible linear map $F$, real $\lambda$ and vector $E_3$. It verifies the required consequence of the choice; identifying $F$ with the parent deformation is not part of this theorem.

e03-s6-growing-initial-direction.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl: The formal condition prescribes the new initial amplitude as a positive scalar multiple of $-E_1(t_0)/S+E_2(t_0)$. The frame and $S>0$ come from the preceding wave. This specifies the direction of a proposed growing wave. Existence is a separate theorem.

e03-s6-growing-peak-normalization.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl: The paper fixes the attained peak at $\lambda^{-3/4}$. The formal condition instead has an independent prescribed peak $U_*$ and requires the maximum on $[t_0,t_0+\Theta/r]$ to equal $U_*$. Recovering this normalization requires setting $U_*=\lambda^{-3/4}$ and $\Theta=r(T-t_0)$; that substitution is not made by this declaration itself.

For a differentiable trace-free $B$ and a nonzero transverse preceding wave on $[t_0,T]$, the formal inequality bounds the comparison error by $8 igl((T-t_0)(M^2+D)/\eta+M/r+E/
u igr)$ for any uniform bounds $M\ge\|B\|_\infty$, $D\ge\|B_t\|_\infty$ and $E\ge\|E_c\|_\infty$, with $r>0$ and $0<\eta\le
u$. The quantity on the left is defined in the formalization as the four suprema of (2.6) in the frame of the preceding wave, with $
u,\eta$ frozen at $t_0$. The explicit constant and the arbitrary upper bounds make this a stronger form of (6.6).

e03-s6-frame-speed.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.movingFrame_: For nonzero perpendicular vectors solving the wave equations over trace-free $B$ at a time in any time set, the formal result gives $|E_i^{\prime}(t)|\le2\|B(t)\|$ for each of the three frame vectors, with derivatives taken within that set. Bounding the pointwise norm by its interval supremum gives the quoted estimate.

e03-s6-later-origin-bounds.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl: To use the paper's $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a|$, take $\lambda>0$ and multiply both amplitude denominators by this same positive factor. The coupling inequality in the quoted display is a separate conclusion.

u=E_1\cdot BE_2>0$, $\eta=E_3\cdot BE_2>0$, and put $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$, $\varepsilon=\eta/
u$. For proposed growing-wave data on $[t_0,t_0+\Theta/r]$, the formal condition requires nonzero transverse vectors $\kappa,\mathbf a$ and $
u_+(t)=(\kappa/|\kappa|)\cdot M(\mathbf a/|\mathbf a|)\ge
u\varepsilon/2$ throughout that interval. It does not require the propagation estimate for every transverse solution in the same display. It specifies properties of supplied data. The existence of data satisfying them is proved separately.

e03-s6-origin-hypotheses.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl: The constant $252e$ is explicit and independent of the wave data, whereas the paper writes an unspecified absolute $C$. Dividing the second inequality by $|\kappa||\mathbf a|>0$ gives the stated coupling bound.

e03-s6-switch-formula.TorusEuler.waveSwitch_eq_one_sub_envelop: Let $\theta:\mathbb R\to[0,1]$ be the fixed smooth transition, zero on $(-\infty,0]$ and one on $[1,\infty)$, and put $\chi(s)=1-\theta(s-1)$ and $\widetilde\chi(t)=\theta(r(t-t_0))$. For every real $r,t_0,t$, the formal statement gives $\widetilde\chi(t)=1-\chi(1+r(t-t_0))$. This is the formula on the positive-time branch in the display. The assertion that it is zero before activation follows separately from the transition's zero region when $r\ge0$; that assertion is not this identity's conclusion.
e03-s6-switch-formula.TorusEuler.waveSwitch_eq_zero_of_le: Let $\theta:\mathbb R\to[0,1]$ be the fixed smooth transition, zero for nonpositive arguments, and set $\widetilde\chi(t)=\theta(r(t-t_0))$. For every $r\ge0$, $t_0\in\mathbb R$ and $t\le t_0$, the formal statement gives $\widetilde\chi(t)=0$. It includes the activation time and the degenerate rate $r=0$. This supplies only the zero branch of the paper's displayed formula. The other branch is a separate identity.

e03-s6-switch-smooth.TorusEuler.contDiff_waveSwitch: Let $\theta:\mathbb R\to[0,1]$ be the fixed smooth transition, zero on $(-\infty,0]$ and one on $[1,\infty)$. For every real $r,t_0$, the formal statement proves that $\widetilde\chi(t)=\theta(r(t-t_0))$ is smooth on all of $\mathbb R$. The paper's positive-rate activation cutoff is this same function, with $\chi(s)=1-\theta(s-1)$. Nonpositive rates are also allowed by the smoothness assertion; only positive rates have the paper's switching-on interpretation.

e03-s6-switch-complete.TorusEuler.waveSwitch_eq_one_of_activati: Let $r>0$ and $\widetilde\chi(t)=\theta(r(t-t_0))$, where the fixed smooth transition $\theta$ equals one on $[1,\infty)$. If $t\ge t_0+1/r$, then the formal statement gives $\widetilde\chi(t)=1$. Since $\tau=r(t-t_0)$, the time hypothesis is exactly $\tau\ge1$. The endpoint $t=t_0+1/r$ is included. This matches the quoted assertion for the paper's activation cutoff.

e03-s6-switch-derivative.TorusEuler.waveSwitch_weighted_derivativ: For the fixed smooth transition $\theta$, set $\widetilde\chi(t)=\theta(r(t-t_0))$. One constant $C\ge0$ is chosen before $t_0$, $r$, $G$ and the weight. Whenever $r>0$, $G\ge0$ and $|\gamma(t)|\le G$ on $[t_0,t_0+1/r]$, the formal statement gives $|\widetilde\chi'(t)\gamma(t)|\le CrG$ for every real $t$. The derivative of the cutoff vanishes outside that interval, so no regularity or bound on the weight there is needed. Choosing $\gamma\equiv1$ and $G=1$ gives the paper's bound $|\widetilde\chi'|\le Cr$.

e03-s6-early-normalized-gain.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl: The constructed wave has maximum amplitude $\lambda^{-3/4}$. The clock sends the physical interval $[t_0,t_0+1/r]$ to the first normalized time unit, where the wave is exponentially smaller than its peak. Multiplying by $\lambda^{3/4}$ gives the bound for $\gamma$ in (6.8).

For proposed growing-wave data over $M=B+\mathbf a_p\otimes\kappa_p+E_c$, let $\varepsilon=\eta/\nu>0$ be the frozen coupling ratio and $r=\sqrt{2\sigma\nu}>0$ the time scale. The formal condition requires $|\mathbf a(t)|\le e^{3-\varepsilon^{-1/2}}U_*$ for $t\in[t_0,t_0+1/r]$, where $U_*$ is an independent prescribed, attained maximum of the seed on $[t_0,t_0+\Theta/r]$. The paper uses $U_*=\lambda^{-3/4}$ and $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a|$, so its displayed normalized estimate follows after that substitution with $\lambda>0$. This declaration describes required data, including the stated early bound. It does not establish their existence.

e03-s6-small-switch-residual.TorusEuler.waveSwitch_weighted_derivativ: Let $\widetilde\chi(t)=\theta(r(t-t_0))$ be the fixed smooth activation cutoff, with $r>0$. One constant $C\ge0$, depending only on $\theta$, works for every weight satisfying $|\gamma(t)|\le G$ on $[t_0,t_0+1/r]$, where $G\ge0$: the formal conclusion is $|\widetilde\chi'(t)\gamma(t)|\le CrG$ for all real $t$. Taking $G=e^{3-\varepsilon^{-1/2}}$ with $\varepsilon>0$ gives the displayed residual factor once the early-gain estimate for $\gamma$ is supplied. The cutoff derivative is zero outside the switching interval, so the theorem imposes no regularity or bound on the weight there.

r2-s6-crossing-input.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl: From the growing launch and the small coefficient-error comparison, the theorem gives a crossing in the stated bracket if $0<\varepsilon_+\le\varepsilon/32$ and the interval reaches $2/\sqrt{\varepsilon\varepsilon_+}$. The construction chooses the least crossing within this bracket in a separate step.

e03-s6-first-crossing.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl: The comparison theorem gives a nonempty set of crossing times in the bracket $[\tau_m,2/\sqrt{\varepsilon\varepsilon_+}]$. The inductive construction chooses the least time within that bracket and converts it to physical time $t_0+\tau/r$. The existence theorem alone supplies a crossing with the required quantitative bounds.

Let $r>0$ be the frozen time scale, $\varepsilon>0$ the preceding coupling ratio and $\varepsilon_+>0$ the prescribed next ratio. For proposed growing-wave data, the formal condition requires a zero $\tau_m\in[2/\varepsilon,3/\varepsilon]$ of the reference slope and a physical crossing time $t_c$ in $[t_0+\tau_m/r,t_0+2(\varepsilon\varepsilon_+)^{-1/2}/r]$. At $t_c$, $\eta_+/\nu_+=\varepsilon_+$; for every other time in this same bracket with that ratio, $t_c$ is no later. These clauses specify exactly the first crossing within the bracket. Existence of data satisfying the clauses is a separate theorem.

r2-s6-reference-turn.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.PhysicalAmpl: This crossing theorem supplies a reference turning time $\tau_m\in[2/\varepsilon,3/\varepsilon]$ and puts the physical crossing after it. The reference amplitude peaks there because its logarithmic derivative changes from positive to negative. The declaration about the crossing itself uses the bounds on $\tau_m$ and assumes a compatible comparison window.

r3c8-s7-central-wave-provenance.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71StepData: The paper identifies both $\mathbf a_j$ and $\kappa_j$ as the central data of the localized wave. The formal step condition identifies the central amplitude with the seed but does not require $\kappa_j(t)=(D_aX_{j-1}(t,0))^{-T}k_*$. Nor does it include the first-wave directions and attained normalization. Those identifications cannot be inferred from this condition alone.

e03-s7-central-couplings.TorusEuler.MovingWaveVector.entry: The formal definition gives a general entry $E_i\cdot M E_j$ for a supplied frame and matrix. It gives the displayed couplings only after choosing the normalized wave frame and $M=\nabla U_{j-1}(t,0)$; neither choice is part of this definition.
e03-s7-central-couplings.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: The formal requirements substitute exactly the normalized central-wave frame and $\nabla U_{j-1}(t,0)$ into the coupling formulas at the crossing time $t=t_{j+1}$. The paper defines the two functions for all times on the active interval. Moreover, these requirements alone do not identify the central covector with the transported covector of the localized expansion.

r2-s7-actual-oscillation.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71StepData: The formal condition identifies the supplied time cutoff with $\widetilde\chi_j$ on $[0,S_j]$ and identifies $O_j$ with the physical evaluation of the expansion minus its phase average on the same interval. This states the two defining identities. It does not prove that step data satisfying them exist.
r2-s7-actual-oscillation.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Steps: For fixed envelope exponent and Fourier symbol, this condition requires suitable expansion data at every $j\ge1$, including the equality of the time cutoffs and $O_j=W_{\rm osc}^{\natural}$ on $[0,S_j]$. The numbered Theorem 7.1 proves the existence of a construction satisfying it.

adapted.E3-S6-01.1.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: The stage construction has $t_1=t_2=0$. The first cutoff is already one, while the second follows the activation profile from that same time. Equal launch times therefore leave the first wave in place as the second is introduced.

e03-s7-half-length.TorusEuler.PaperTheorem71Conclusions: The formal assertion has $t_1=t_2=0$, $S_0=1$ and $S_j=t_j+2\tau_j$ for every $j\ge1$, with $\tau_j=\lambda_{j-1}^{-1/8}(4\log\lambda_{j+2})^3$. This is the displayed formula since $L_{j+1}=4\log\lambda_{j+2}$.
e03-s7-half-length.TorusEuler.paperTheorem71: The formal assertion has $t_1=t_2=0$, $S_0=1$ and $S_j=t_j+2\tau_j$ for every $j\ge1$, with $\tau_j=\lambda_{j-1}^{-1/8}(4\log\lambda_{j+2})^3$. This is the displayed formula since $L_{j+1}=4\log\lambda_{j+2}$.
e03-s7-half-length.TorusEuler.Paper.Schedule.τ: This definition gives $\tau_j=\lambda_{j-1}^{-1/8}L_{j+1}^3$ for positive wave indices. The display also gives the initial activation times and final times, which are not part of this definition. Its additional value at index zero uses zero in place of a negative index and is unused by the paper.
e03-s7-half-length.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: The formal assertion has $t_1=t_2=0$, $S_0=1$ and $S_j=t_j+2\tau_j$ for every $j\ge1$, with $\tau_j=\lambda_{j-1}^{-1/8}(4\log\lambda_{j+2})^3$. This is the displayed formula since $L_{j+1}=4\log\lambda_{j+2}$.

e03-s7-depth.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.step: The internal step index $i$ builds wave $j=i+1$. Its depth is $6K(q_{i+2})=6K_{j+1}$, so the apparent extra index shift is exactly the paper's choice. Both the depth and derivative orders are nonnegative integers.

e03-s7-existence.TorusEuler.paperTheorem71: The paper fixes the construction constants before allowing any admissible majorant $\mathcal B$. This theorem proves existence for one selected threshold function and omits the explicit Section 5 expansion identities. It still constructs a common sequence for every sufficiently large $N$ for that selection.
e03-s7-existence.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1: For a fixed admissible Fourier symbol and any integer floor $a_0$, the formal statement chooses integers $b\ge1$ and $a\ge a_0$ and fixed-order majorants before $\mathcal B$. Every admissible $\mathcal B$ then has a threshold above which every $N$ yields one common construction and increasing activation times. The remaining differences in its central-wave identifications are discussed at those clauses.
e03-s7-existence.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: For a fixed admissible Fourier symbol and any integer floor $a_0$, the formal statement chooses integers $b\ge1$ and $a\ge a_0$ and fixed-order majorants before $\mathcal B$. Every admissible $\mathcal B$ then has a threshold above which every $N$ yields one common construction and increasing activation times. The remaining differences in its central-wave identifications are discussed at those clauses.

r2-s7-shear-identification.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: The formal requirement is $U_0(t,x)=\sin(2\pi x_2)(e_1+\varepsilon_1e_3)$ for every real $t$, with $\varepsilon_1=(4\log\lambda_3)^{-2}$. This is exactly the shear used in the paper's construction, represented as a periodic field on $\mathbb R^3$.
r2-s7-shear-identification.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1: The formal requirement is $U_0(t,x)=\sin(2\pi x_2)(e_1+\varepsilon_1e_3)$ for every real $t$, with $\varepsilon_1=(4\log\lambda_3)^{-2}$. This is exactly the shear used in the paper's construction, represented as a periodic field on $\mathbb R^3$.

e03-s7-T1.TorusEuler.paperTheorem71: For every sufficiently large starting frequency, this theorem constructs stages whose velocity has a finite Fourier band. At stage $j$ the outer radius is $2\lambda_j^5=2\Lambda_j$. Thus each next wave starts from a parent with controlled spatial frequencies.
e03-s7-T1.TorusEuler.PaperTheorem71Conclusions: The field `stage_regular` requires smoothness on the closed stage interval and periodicity, oddness and zero divergence at every time. It also requires the torus Fourier support to lie in the stated band. This proof record is a condition on a supplied sequence.
e03-s7-T1.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: The field `T1` uses functions on $\mathbb R^3$ to state smoothness and oddness, then uses their periodic torus representatives for the frequency bound. The factor $2$ in the radius matches the cutoff symbol's support at twice the chosen scale.
e03-s7-T1.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1: The statement quantifies over a smooth cutoff symbol in advance and asks for a sequence satisfying T1 with that cutoff. Its stage velocities are all divergence free and have Fourier band $2\lambda_j^5$, so the same band condition passes to the next parent.
e03-s7-T1.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: The proved numbered theorem gives T1 for every stage of the selected construction. In particular the Fourier support is bounded after the wave and corrections are assembled, since the stage is the output of the prescribed cutoff.

e03-s7-T2.TorusEuler.paperTheorem71: The selected construction controls the velocity and both directions of its particle deformation at scale $\lambda_j$. The residual needs the tighter scale $\lambda_{j+1}^{-3}$, because the first mean correction of the next stage has to cancel it.
e03-s7-T2.TorusEuler.PaperTheorem71Conclusions: The field `stage_size` records two derivative maps $F$ and $G$ at corresponding forward and reverse particle positions. They are inverse maps with norm at most $\lambda_j$. It also bounds the pointwise residual by the inverse cube of the next frequency.
e03-s7-T2.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: In field `T2`, the forward and inverse derivative bounds are packaged as a deformation condition on the stage flow. The velocity and residual bounds are stated pointwise at every stage time, which gives the two uniform norms in the passage.
e03-s7-T2.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1: T2 is required of the sequence produced for an admissible threshold and sufficiently large $N$. The first two bounds protect the flow estimates at the current frequency, while the residual is measured against the next one. Both stage-dependent scales are part of the conclusion.
e03-s7-T2.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: The proof obtains all three estimates for the same stage and the same flow. The inverse deformation bound uses the reverse flow at the transported point. The residual bound is on the actual Euler momentum defect of that selected velocity and pressure.

e03-s7-T4-splitting.TorusEuler.paperTheorem71: The constructed stages have a central derivative equal to the preceding derivative plus one cutoff-weighted rank-one shear and a small operator error. The exact equality uses the central wave in the conclusion record. Identifying its normal with the localized profile's normal is an additional assertion.
e03-s7-T4-splitting.TorusEuler.PaperTheorem71Conclusions: The field `central_gradient` writes the rank-one term as the map $v\mapsto(\kappa_j\cdot v)\mathbf a_j$ times the cutoff. Its error bound is an operator norm at the origin for the active time window. The record uses the stored central normal.
e03-s7-T4-splitting.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: The field `T4_gradient` subtracts the previous stage's gradient before measuring the new shear and error at zero. The error is at most $\lambda_j^{-1/4}$. The central covector appearing there is a field of the central wave data.
e03-s7-T4-splitting.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1: The numbered statement combines the central splitting with a finite-expansion condition for each stage. It identifies the central amplitude with the expansion's seed, and the splitting is written with the central wave's stored covector. Equality of that covector with the transported one is a separate condition.
e03-s7-T4-splitting.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: The proof gives the central splitting on the same interval used for the new wave. The small error controls what is lost when using the rank-one term to compute the next wave's couplings. The theorem identifies the central amplitude with the selected seed.

e03-s7-T4-clock.TorusEuler.paperTheorem71: The construction reaches its selected next activation by time $t_j+\tau_j$. The current cutoff equals one from that activation until $S_j$. This makes the full shear available to the successor at its start.
e03-s7-T4-clock.TorusEuler.PaperTheorem71Conclusions: The field `crossing_window` uses the stage half-length as an upper bound on the elapsed physical time. It records unit cutoff throughout the remaining interval, so the central splitting has no cutoff loss there.
e03-s7-T4-clock.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: The field `T4_times` records the time gap and the cutoff value separately. Combining it with $S_j=t_j+2\tau_j$ leaves at least the other half-length of the stage after the next launch.
e03-s7-T4-clock.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1: The statement requires this cutoff conclusion from the next activation through the end of the current stage. Its independent first-cutoff requirement also covers the initial case $t_1=t_2=0$, where the interval between launches has length zero.
e03-s7-T4-clock.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: The theorem supplies both the timely crossing and a completed cutoff at that crossing for the chosen waves. The crossing time alone would allow a partial cutoff. The second clause is what gives the next amplitude equation the unattenuated central shear.

e03-s7-crossing-values.TorusEuler.paperTheorem71: At the selected launch of the successor the present wave's central coupling ratio is the prescribed one. The theorem keeps its first coupling between $\pi$ and $4\pi$ while retaining shear of order at least $\lambda_j^{1/4}$. These are conclusions about the same selected crossing.
e03-s7-crossing-values.TorusEuler.PaperTheorem71Conclusions: The field `crossing_values` reads the two entries of the previous gradient in the current central wave's frame at the next activation. It calculates $\sigma_j$ as amplitude length times wave-normal length, then bounds it with the strength constant stored in the construction.
e03-s7-crossing-values.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: The field `T4_late_values` uses the same central frame for all three clauses of (7.3). Its $\nu_j$ bound ensures division by a positive number when forming the prescribed ratio. The shear bounds are on the central amplitude-normal product.
e03-s7-crossing-values.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1: The statement fixes the strength constant at $18e^3$ and asserts the ratio and shear bounds at the chosen crossing. Its stage data make the central amplitude the localized seed. The central normal and the transported covector have separate declarations.
e03-s7-crossing-values.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: The proof preserves a positive first coupling and large central shear at the time when the smaller target ratio is reached. The powers in (7.3) allow the successor to start with both sufficient strength and the specified orientation in the central frame.

e03-s7-lifetime.TorusEuler.paperTheorem71: The construction produces one positive real limit of the activation times and keeps that limit below all stage endpoints. The same terminal time can therefore be used to compare every approximate velocity, including the earliest ones.
e03-s7-lifetime.TorusEuler.PaperTheorem71Conclusions: The `lifetime` field consists of positivity, convergence of the activation sequence and the strict endpoint inequalities. It permits evaluation at the common limit in every stage's own time domain. This condition is on the approximate sequence.
e03-s7-lifetime.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: For the supplied construction, `lifetime` gives $t_j\to T$ in the real numbers, with $0<T<S_j$ for each index. The strict inequality distinguishes the shared accumulation time from any individual stage endpoint.
e03-s7-lifetime.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1: In the numbered statement the same existential time $T$ appears in all of the stage conclusions. It is positive, finite, and less than every $S_j$. Identifying it with the lifespan of the exact Euler solution is done after taking the limit.
e03-s7-lifetime.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: The selected stages all extend past the accumulation of their launch times. This puts $T_\infty$ in every approximate solution's time interval, so the velocity can be compared there before any conclusion about the limiting equation at that time.

e03-s7-oscillation-support.TorusEuler.paperTheorem71: The formal assertion places its chosen oscillation within distance $\lambda_{j-1}^{-1}$ of the integer lattice at each time in $[0,S_j]$, which is the stated torus ball. This assertion alone does not identify that oscillation with the finite expansion $W_{\rm osc}^{\natural}$; the numbered theorem supplies that identity through additional step data.

This assertion alone does not identify that oscillation with the finite expansion $W_{\rm osc}^{\natural}$; the numbered theorem supplies that identity through additional step data.
e03-s7-oscillation-support.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1: The formal theorem identifies $O_j=W_{\rm osc}^{\natural}$ through the step data and gives $O_j(t,x)\ne0\Rightarrow\operatorname{dist}(x,\mathbb Z^3)\le\lambda_{j-1}^{-1}$ on $[0,S_j]$. Integer translates of the origin in the lift represent the single origin of the torus, so this is precisely the paper's support assertion.
e03-s7-oscillation-support.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: The formal theorem identifies $O_j=W_{\rm osc}^{\natural}$ through the step data and gives $O_j(t,x)\ne0\Rightarrow\operatorname{dist}(x,\mathbb Z^3)\le\lambda_{j-1}^{-1}$ on $[0,S_j]$. Integer translates of the origin in the lift represent the single origin of the torus, so this is precisely the paper's support assertion.

e03-s7-increment-bounds.TorusEuler.paperTheorem71: The constructed increment separates a localized oscillation small in supremum norm from a remainder small in spatial $C^{m,1/2}$ through the scheduled order. The bounds are uniform over the stage in time. The off-origin argument uses the improved derivative bounds on the remainder after the oscillation's support leaves a compact set.
e03-s7-increment-bounds.TorusEuler.PaperTheorem71Conclusions: The fields `oscillation_small` and `increment` apply at every time. The first controls $O_j$ and the second takes the spatial Hölder norm only after subtracting $O_j$ from the stage difference. The separated fields record bounds on time slices.
e03-s7-increment-bounds.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: The `increment` field gives spatial Hölder regularity and a norm bound through $q_j$ once the leading oscillation is removed. Its $C^{m,1/2}$ condition is at each time. Continuity as a curve in that space is a separate regularity consequence.
e03-s7-increment-bounds.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1: The statement asks for both estimates from the same chosen sequence, with the expansion specifying which term is $O_j$. The uniform bounds are expressed pointwise in stage time. The supremum bound on $O_j$ alone does not control its higher spatial derivatives.
e03-s7-increment-bounds.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: The proof makes both parts of the stage increment small at scale $\lambda_j^{-1}$. The leading oscillation uses the weaker supremum norm while the rest carries spatial derivative control through $q_j$. This distinction lets the construction gain large central derivatives while summing the velocity increments.

e03-s7-inactive-oscillation.TorusEuler.paperTheorem71: The formal assertion requires its chosen oscillation to be zero on $[0,t_j]$ for every $j\ge2$, including activation. Its conclusion alone does not identify this field with the actual expansion oscillation named in the paper. That identification is additional data in the numbered theorem.
e03-s7-inactive-oscillation.TorusEuler.PaperTheorem71Conclusions: The formal assertion requires its chosen oscillation to be zero on $[0,t_j]$ for every $j\ge2$, including activation. Its conclusion alone does not identify this field with the actual expansion oscillation named in the paper. That identification is additional data in the numbered theorem.
e03-s7-inactive-oscillation.TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions: The formal assertion requires its chosen oscillation to be zero on $[0,t_j]$ for every $j\ge2$, including activation. Its conclusion alone does not identify this field with the actual expansion oscillation named in the paper. That identification is additional data in the numbered theorem.
e03-s7-inactive-oscillation.TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1: The formal theorem identifies the step's actual expansion oscillation $O_j$ and requires $O_j(t)=0$ for every $t\in[0,t_j]$ when $j\ge2$. This includes the endpoint where the cutoff and the higher profiles have zero initial data.
e03-s7-inactive-oscillation.TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1: The formal theorem identifies the step's actual expansion oscillation $O_j$ and requires $O_j(t)=0$ for every $t\in[0,t_j]$ when $j\ge2$. This includes the endpoint where the cutoff and the higher profiles have zero initial data.
