Repeating that identity yields the higher powers in the passage when the profiles are smooth.

e03-aux-factorial-convolution.TorusEuler.terminalTimeJetWeight_mul_cho: The identity factors $(T^n/n!)\binom ni$ into $T^i/i!$ and $T^{n-i}/(n-i)!$. These are the weights of the two derivative orders in Leibniz' rule, so the weighted derivative bound has the ordinary convolution coefficients.
e03-aux-factorial-convolution.TorusEuler.terminalTimeConvolution_le: Weight each derivative term by $T^i/i!$. The binomial coefficient from Leibniz' rule then distributes the weight across the two factors. The formal scalar bound sums that convolution, after the spatial estimate has bounded each product by the product of seminorms.

e03-r2-aux-mean-differentiated-equation.TorusEuler.terminalProjectedHigherTimeDe: The formal identity assumes an integrated equation $P(Kv)=c+P\int_0^t(\Omega v+g)$ and differentiates it, with $P$ any bounded linear map. The paper uses the Leray projection and $\mathcal D=2(D_aX)^T\partial_tD_aX$. Recovering its display requires $\Omega=K_t-\mathcal D$, the identity (M.4.2), followed by the binomial rearrangement. The general formal identity does not itself impose those geometric identifications.

e03-r2-aux-mean-time-gain-display.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex: The formal estimate controls mean velocity at time order $q$ by the source at order $q-1$ for $q\ge1$, with one extra label derivative on the source. The gain comes from recovering time derivatives of the mean velocity from its equation. The parent-scale factor pays for the coefficients.

e03-r2-aux-transverse-time-bound.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex: The theorem supplies this forcing-to-velocity estimate for the selected transverse levels between two and $P$ under parent bounds and a sufficiently small envelope. It controls their time derivatives using the force budget. Estimating the corresponding oscillatory pressure requires its formula separately.

e03-r2-aux-residual-time-source-bound.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.sc: The time-source estimate supplies the $R_U\circ X$ part of $\bar f_2$, retaining the $\lambda^{-5/2}$ power in the norm at time order $q-1$. To bound the full source at spatial order $n+1$ one must also estimate the phase-averaged stress.

e03-r2-aux-mean-source-order.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te: The measurement definition pairs a mean velocity estimate of time order $q$ with a mean source of order $\max(q-1,0)$. For positive $q$ this gives the one-order difference in the passage. At zero it uses the undifferentiated source.

e03-aux-recurrence-smallness.TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.even: Substituting $\lambda=\mu^{K_j}$ turns the smallness expression into $C\mu^{A-K_j/12}$. As $K_j$ grows, the exponent eventually beats the fixed parent power, including the constant for any fixed derivative order. The required stage can depend on those fixed choices.

e03-aux-hierarchy-time-lift.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex: The selected expansion has bounds in the time norms for its total oscillation, mean, depth remainder and activation correction. The theorem assumes the parent time bounds and smallness conditions. Its single parent exponent works for all the spatial orders allowed by the derivative budget, with constants depending on the order.

e03-r2-aux-aggregate-expansion-rates.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Sc: The formal condition records the decay factors separately for the total oscillation, mean and remainder of the finite expansion. Its bound is available when $n+3P\le H$, where $H$ is the spatial derivative allowance. The theorem that supplies those bounds increases this allowance along the selected stages.

e03-r2-aux-oscillatory-spatial-cost.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi: The theorem verifies the numerical step $\mathsf D^{\max(a,1)+1}\lambda^{3/2}\le\lambda^2$ when the displayed parent factor is at most $\lambda^{1/2}$. A spatial chain-rule estimate supplies the factor on the left. The phase-independent derivative estimate is a separate part of the passage.

c8-auxiliary-mean-polynomial-absorption.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Po: This condition records a bound $\mu^B\lambda^{-5/2}$ for a selected mean's fixed Eulerian time derivative in the formal spatial Hölder norm. It does not prove that bound, assert continuity in time, or give the second inequality $\tfrac12\lambda^{-1}$. The integer exponent and stage are specified inputs.
c8-auxiliary-mean-polynomial-absorption.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te: The formal implication absorbs a fixed parent power once the analytic mean and approximation estimates are assumed to follow from the preceding time-order bounds. It then gives the half-size mean estimate eventually at each fixed pair of orders. It does not prove the analytic premises of (2.4).

e03-aux-physical-time-estimates.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.po: The formal theorem first gives $\mu^B\lambda^{2(n+1)+2q}$ for velocity derivatives and $\mu^B\lambda^{2(q+2)}\lambda_{j+1}^{-4}$ for the residual, under explicit parent, inverse-flow, activation and derivative-reserve hypotheses. The paper's display has already absorbed the parent power into $\psi'_q$. That absorption is a subsequent step, not the conclusion at this link.

e03-r2-aux-tail-depth-identity.TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi: With $\lambda>0$, $P=6K$ and $\lambda_{j+1}=\lambda^K$, the formal identity rewrites $\lambda^{-5/4-2P/3}$ as $\lambda^{-5/4}\lambda_{j+1}^{-4}$. Cancelling the positive factor $\lambda^{-5/4}$ gives exactly the equality quoted here. The theorem is arithmetic and supplies no analytic estimate for $R_P$.

e03-aux-cutoff-commutation.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ: The formal theorem proves $\partial_t^q(S_{\Lambda_j}V)=S_{\Lambda_j}\partial_t^qV$ for the fixed spatial cutoff, with smooth periodic representatives of the time derivatives on the closed slab. Subtracting $\partial_t^qV$ gives the paper's formula for $v_\Lambda$. The linked conclusion itself is the cutoff-velocity identity.

e03-aux-cutoff-tail-estimate.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ: For $m\le P$ and $\Lambda>0$, the formal theorem gives $C_P\Lambda^{m-P}\|\partial_t^qV(t)\|_{C^{P,1/2}}$ as a spatial tail bound. It has not substituted $C_P\le\mu$, $\Lambda=\lambda^5$ or the approximate-velocity estimate. Those substitutions produce the paper's displayed expression. Time continuity in the norm is also supplied separately.

e03-aux-half-tail.TorusEuler.terminalTime_cutoff_tail_rate: The formal result is a single-stage numerical implication: if $\lambda\ge2$, $C\le\lambda$ and $5m+5+\psi'_q\le3P$, then the cutoff expression is at most $\tfrac12\lambda^{-1}$. It does not itself prove that these hypotheses hold at all sufficiently large stages. That uses the schedule and the fact that $m,q$ are fixed.

e03-aux-exact-correction-split.TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se: For each selected later step, the formal equality identifies the correction with the actual mean of that step plus its actual Fourier-cutoff error. Its indexing starts with $j=2$. The equality is between the globally defined fields. The auxiliary estimates apply on the closed interval $[0,S_j]$.

e03-aux-add-half-bounds.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ: Given a smooth split $V=U+O+M$, the explicit depth condition for the cutoff tail and a half-size mean bound, the formal theorem gives $\|\partial_t^q(S_\Lambda V-U-O)\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le\lambda^{-1}$ at the chosen time. It does not provide the eventual starting stage or continuity in the spatial norm required by the full auxiliary Lemma 1.2.

e03-aux-new-velocity-power.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ: Let $V$ be smooth and periodic on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$, with $T>0$, and use the selected fixed cutoff at $\Lambda=\lambda^5$. At a specified time and order $i$, assume $\lambda\ge2$, $1+C_0\le\lambda$ for the fixed order-zero cutoff constant, and $\|\partial_t^iV\|_{C^{0,1/2}}\le\lambda^{2+\psi'_q}$. The formal statement gives $|\partial_t^iU_j(t,x)|\le\lambda^{\psi'_q+3}$ for every $x$. The derivatives are within the closed time interval. Applying the statement at every $i\le q$ and every time gives the quoted supremum bound. The needed approximate-velocity estimates remain hypotheses.

e03-r2-aux-cutoff-residual-identity.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ: The formal theorem gives every time derivative of the residual as the Leray projection of the differentiated cutoff residual and a binomial sum of quadratic cutoff errors. At order zero its tensor error is $U_j\otimes U_j-S(V\otimes V)$. With $v=U_j-V$, this equals the three tensors displayed in the paper. The cutoff symbol and scale are fixed in time.

e03-aux-new-residual-power.TorusEuler.slabTimeJet_cutoffResidual_ra: The formal result proves $|\partial_t^iR_j(t,x)|\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-5/2}$ from an assumed analytic residual-error bound and explicit inequalities including $\lambda_{j+1}=\lambda_j^K$ and $K\ge16+2\psi'_q$. It is a pointwise implication at a specified order and time. The eventual validity of those assumptions and continuity in the spatial supremum norm are separate parts of the full lemma.

e03-aux-oscillations-leave-compact.TorusEuler.inductive_oscillations_eventu: A compact set away from the lattice has positive distance from it. Once the support radii are smaller than a fraction of that distance, an open neighborhood of the compact set misses the support of every later oscillation at every stage time. The theorem isolates this geometric fact from the Euler estimates.
